name: Keyboard and IME events
plain: Sees every key pressed while the page has focus, plus IME composition text.
meaning: A page that has focus gets each keydown with the key and its physical code, and exact timing. Typing rhythm can identify a person; composition events reveal the language they type in.

web.api: keydown, keyup, beforeinput, input, compositionstart/update/end; KeyboardEvent.key, .code, .timeStamp

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Keys go to the focused frame only; cross-origin iframes do not leak keys to the parent
steps: Page reads key, code, isComposing and data

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.precision: 100 us in Chrome, about 1 ms in Firefox and Safari

limits.headline: Can see each key you press while the page has focus
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you type while the page is open and in front
can: See which key you pressed and the exact time
Tell the difference between a typed letter and a shortcut like Ctrl plus C
Learn your typing rhythm, which can help tell people apart
See text from input method editors, which can show the language you type in
cannot: See keys pressed in other tabs or other apps
See anything while the page is in the background
Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.reach_label: Every key while the page is open

story.what_it_is: The page sees every key you press while it is focused, including timing.
story.for_you: You press keys and the page reacts: a game character moves, a shortcut opens a menu, a search box suggests words. You do not see that each key and its exact timing was noticed. The page only sees keys while it is the active window.
story.for_makers: Keys drive games, shortcuts, forms and chat. Makers also use typing speed and rhythm for fraud and bot checks, and some analytics tools record keystrokes in forms.

use_cases.example: A browser shooter reads WASD, space and shift every frame so your character moves and jumps.
A cloud gaming site such as GeForce NOW sends each key press to the remote machine to play a PC game in the browser.
A design tool uses key shortcuts such as V for move and Space to pan.
A bank login checks typing rhythm to judge whether the same person is typing as always.
A session recording tool replays how visitors typed in a form and where they gave up.
A bot detector flags forms filled in perfectly even typing speed with no pauses.
A web app offers keyboard only control for people who cannot use a mouse.

technical_bounds: No key events for text typed in other tabs, apps, the address bar or OS dialogs
Event timeStamp is a DOMHighResTimeStamp: 100 microseconds in Chrome, coarser in Firefox and Safari (about 1 ms)
Password fields still fire keydown (the page owner can read what is typed there)
During IME composition keydown carries key Process (keyCode 229); the composed text comes through compositionend and beforeinput
Browsers cannot hide key timing; keystroke dynamics identify users at roughly 1 to 5 percent equal error rate in research

abuse: Keylogging typed form data in injected scripts
